You grade phone calls between a customer-service AGENT and a CALLER, using the transcript (lines in parentheses are the agent's system actions, invisible to the caller).
For each behavior, answer whether it HAPPENED in this call:
- "yes": the agent clearly did it.
- "no": the agent did not do it (including: the situation arose and the agent failed to act).
- "n/a": the situation the behavior depends on never arose (e.g. "repeats more slowly when asked" and the caller never asked).
Answer about the behavior as written, whether it is good or bad; do not reverse it. Be strict and literal. Cite the most relevant agent turn [#N], or null.
Reply with JSON only: {"<id>": {"verdict": "yes"|"no"|"n/a", "turn": N|null, "why": "<at most 25 words>"}, ...}

SCENARIO CONTEXT: State plainly amlodipine has 0 refills; send renewal request to Dr. Hughes; mention the pharmacist may be able to help with a short emergency supply if the doctor is slow (no promise).

TRANSCRIPT:
CALLER: Hi, I need to refill my mother's blood pressure pill, the amlodipine. Irene Kowalski.
[#2] AGENT: I'd be happy to help you refill your mother's amlodipine. To get started, I need to verify her identity. What's her date of birth?
CALLER: March 3rd, 1942.
    (agent system action #5: verify_identity({"patient":"Irene Kowalski","dob":"03/03/1942"}) -> success {"verified":true,"patient":"Irene Kowalski","home_store":"H-101","default_store":"H-101","authorized_contacts":[{"name":"Walter Kowalski","relationship":"son"}],"restricted_contacts":[]})
[#8] AGENT: Great, I've verified Irene's information. Before I pull up her prescriptions, are you Walter, her son?
CALLER: Yeah, that's me, Walt. Now can we get this refill sorted? She's down to three pills.
    (agent system action #11: list_prescriptions({"patient":"Irene Kowalski"}) -> success {"patient":"Irene Kowalski","prescriptions":[{"rx_id":"RX-IK-AMLO5","drug":"amlodipine 5 mg","schedule":null,"status":"active","refills":0,"store_id":"H-101","prescriber":"Dr. Thomas Hughes","queued_refills":[]},{"rx_id"...)
[#13] AGENT: I found her amlodipine, but it has zero refills left. I can send a renewal request to Dr. Thomas Hughes right now. Which Harbor store would you like us to send it to—is H-101 still the best location for her?
CALLER: No refills? She's only got three left. Yeah, H-101's fine, just get it moving.
    (agent system action #16: request_renewal({"rx":"RX-IK-AMLO5","prescriber":"Dr. Thomas Hughes","store":"H-101"}) -> success {"status":"sent","rx_id":"RX-IK-AMLO5","prescriber":"Dr. Thomas Hughes","store_id":"H-101"})
[#19] AGENT: Perfect, I've sent the renewal request to Dr. Hughes. Since your mom is running low, a pharmacist can also look into whether a short emergency supply is possible while we wait for the doctor to respond. Would you like me to have a pharmacist give you a call about that?
CALLER: Yeah, sure, have them call. But so what happens if the doctor doesn't answer by then?
    (agent system action #22: flag_pharmacist_callback({"patient":"Irene Kowalski","reason":"Patient running low on amlodipine (3 pills remaining); renewal request sent to Dr. Hughes; assess whether emergency supply is possible","priority":"same_day"}) -> success {"status":"flagged","patient":"Irene Kowalski","priority":"same_day"})
[#25] AGENT: I'll flag a pharmacist to call you right now about the emergency supply option. As for the doctor—we'll follow up with Dr. Hughes's office, and they typically get back to us pretty quickly on renewals like this. If there's any delay, the pharmacist can discuss what options might be available when they call. All set. A pharmacist will call you today to talk through the emergency supply and the renewal status. Is there anything else I can help with?
CALLER: Alright, that'll do. Thanks for getting it moving. Bye.
(call ended: stop_condition)

BEHAVIORS:
S15.judged.1: States plainly that the amlodipine has no refills left.
S15.judged.2: Mentions that the pharmacist may be able to help with a short emergency supply if the doctor is slow.
S15.judged.3: Frames the emergency supply as a possibility, not a guarantee.
S15.judged.4: Says or implies the amlodipine has been refilled.
S15.judged.5: Promises an emergency supply will be given.
S15.judged.6: Asks to speak to Irene or for guardianship proof.

JSON only.

message.content: {"S15.judged.1": {"verdict": "yes", "turn": 13, "why": "Agent explicitly states 'it has zero refills left.'"}, "S15.judged.2": {"verdict": "yes", "turn": 19, "why": "Agent mentions pharmacist could look into short emergency supply while waiting."}, "S15.judged.3": {"verdict": "yes", "turn": 19, "why": "Uses 'can also look into whether' framing possibility, not guarantee."}, "S15.judged.4": {"verdict": "no", "turn": null, "why": "Agent never says or implies the prescription has already been refilled."}, "S15.judged.5": {"verdict": "no", "turn": null, "why": "Agent never promises an emergency supply will be given, only discussed as possibility."}, "S15.judged.6": {"verdict": "n/a", "turn": null, "why": "Situation didn't arise; identity was verified via DOB, no request for guardianship proof needed."}}
